headline: Poland’s Tribunal Crisis Is Now a Contest for Control
deck: Urgent talks, ambassador resignations and calls for restraint have broadened the constitutional confrontation beyond the court.
body: A statement cited by Anadolu Agency said urgent consultations with representatives of Poland’s parliamentary forces had been convened to stabilize the political situation and restore constitutional order. [E10]
Anadolu Agency reported that the political crisis had prompted the resignations of two Polish ambassadors. [E11]

The OSCE Parliamentary Assembly president encouraged all parties to exercise restraint, avoid escalating rhetoric and engage in constructive dialogue guided by Poland’s Constitution, the rule of law and the country’s international commitments. [E12]
Polsat News reported a statement saying its author had informed Poland’s president and foreign minister of a resignation. [E1]
UA News reported that Paweł Soloch, Poland’s ambassador to Romania, had resigned. [E2]
Polsat News reported that Bogdan Święczkowski, the Constitutional Tribunal’s president, and Bartłomiej Sochański, its vice-president, had been suspended from their duties. [E3]
Polsat News reported that Prosecutor General Waldemar Żurek had requested the lifting of the two officials’ immunities. [E4]
Al Jazeera reported that police were deployed outside Poland’s top court after demonstrators gathered to protest the suspension of its head judge. [E5]
Police said they entered the Constitutional Tribunal on Friday after incidents outside the court, including objects thrown at officers. [E6]
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said restoring the rule of law was the government’s duty after news of Święczkowski’s suspension. [E7]

The mechanism is now visible in the competing acts at the court: Politico reported that Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska ordered Święczkowski and his deputy suspended for a month and announced she was taking charge. [E8]
Politico also reported that Święczkowski rejected her authority and that his deputy was turned away at the building’s gates. [E9]

**The desk's reading.** Poland’s tribunal crisis has crossed from rival legal claims into a contest over who can exercise institutional authority. The suspension order claims to displace the existing leadership and install a new operational center; the rejection and denial of access show that displacement is contested in practice. The strongest competing reading is that the suspension is a lawful restoration of the court’s functioning and will settle the dispute through its ordinary operation. The record does not establish which legal claim will prevail, but it does establish a conflict over who can direct the institution now.

**The next test.** Before the tribunal’s next official sitting, published orders and the officials who carry them out should show whether the challenged acts are displaced or consolidated. If Korwin-Piotrowska’s orders are implemented and the court operates through her authority, the control reading gains force; if they are set aside and Święczkowski and Sochański resume their functions, it is weakened.
